learning_outcomes.text: Understands basic concepts regarding the rules and technique of sports games and gymnastics exercises.
Knows the structure and purpose of the main physical exercises and sports practiced within physical education disciplines.
Understands the role of physical activity in the physical and psychological balance necessary for a demanding engineering career.
Is able to correctly apply technical-tactical elements from athletics, gymnastics, sports games or fitness.
Actively participates in exercises and applied games for the development of basic motor skills.
Demonstrates physical skills and coordination in the execution of individual or group exercises.
Adapts physical effort to one's own capabilities and contributes to team sports activities.
Demonstrates responsibility in respecting regulations, safety norms and instructions from teaching staff.
Demonstrates autonomy in practicing physical exercise outside of class hours.
Adopts correct and collaborative behavior in collective sports activities.
Is aware of the importance of physical education in long-term personal and professional development.

syllabus_topics: Technique of the launched stride and standing start
Front and formation exercises, walking and running variations, simple floor exercises
Game-like exercises and simple dynamic elements from acrobatic gymnastics (rolls, turnovers, etc.)
Applied courses combined with balance, climbing, transport elements
Classical, modern and folk dance steps to appropriate music
Sports games: basketball, handball, football, volleyball, badminton.
Fundamental positions, placement and movement on the field
Simple shots, serves, exercises for receiving, catching and passing the ball from a standstill and while running
Exercises for finishing elementary technical and technical-tactical actions, marking and unmarking exercises
Overall participation in games on reduced and normal fields with different team sizes.
Increase in strength and muscle mass through appropriate and individualized use of weights, dumbbells and barbells
Exercises for shaping and transforming fat into active mass.
Improvement of speed manifestations (reaction, repetition, movement, execution through specific exercises)
Improvement of general coordination indices and specific dexterity for various specific branches
Increase in mobility and flexibility at the level of different segments

assessment_methods.method: Systematic observation of students (individual/team assignments, reports)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result is based on the weighted scores of each activity. Grades are awarded from 1 to 10, with 5 being the minimum passing grade, certifying the achievement of minimal learning outcomes and the awarding of credits. The student passes if they demonstrate fundamental practical skills in athletics, gymnastics, sports games, and bodybuilding/fitness, and the capacity to correctly and efficiently execute specific techniques, participate actively in sports activities, and improve basic and specific motor skills through individualized training. All laboratory works must be completed, with recovery allowed for only one outstanding laboratory work. A minimum grade of 5 is required for the ongoing verification and laboratory components.
